function: SVM, KNN and a feedforward neural network detect QAM symbols after ZF or MMSE equalization; the paper's geometry ratio relates their separability to BER (p. 4, 7).
system: SISO, 2x2, 4x4 and 8x8 MIMO, 16-QAM and 64-QAM, narrowband point-to-point link with perfect CSI, AWGN and Rayleigh fading; no carrier frequency stated (p. 6, 15).
method: Supervised SVM, KNN (k=5) and fully connected NN (128-128-64, 100 epochs, Adam) on Re, Im, magnitude and phase features; geometry ratio itself is non-learned (p. 5, 6).
data_channel: Custom simulation: AWGN and Rayleigh (Hij ~ CN(0,1)) channels, random 16/64-QAM symbols generated per SNR, 5000 samples per SNR, 5 Monte Carlo runs; no external dataset (p. 5, 6, 7).
test_conditions: Data generated independently per SNR (0 to 20 dB), stratified 70%/30% train/test split; same training configuration for every modulation order and MIMO size (p. 5, 6).
baselines: Classical nearest-constellation detection after ZF/MMSE, MMSE-SIC; learned SVM, KNN and NN compared with each other and with classical detection (p. 9, 11, 12).
metrics: BER (primary), classification accuracy, geometry ratio, Pearson, Spearman and partial correlations, R^2 between geometry ratio and BER (p. 3, 13, 14).
q1_support: p. 7: "In the Rayleigh fading channel, each element of the channel matrix follows a complex Gaussian distribution"; custom AWGN and Rayleigh simulator, with no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "The dataset was divided using a stratified 70%/30% (train/test) split"; p. 5: "The datasets were generated independently for each SNR value". Test data follow the training distribution; SNR, modulation and MIMO size are swept with the same training configuration, with no unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 10: "BER comparison between NN, SVM, and KNN in AWGN"; p. 15: "while achieving performance comparable to machine learning and neural network-based approaches" (classical detection versus learned); p. 9: "Perform classical detection (nearest constellation)". Fig. 8a (p. 12) plots the BER of Classical, KNN, SVM and NN.
q4_support: p. 16: "future studies will examine computational complexity, memory requirements, runtime behavior". Only layer sizes are given (Table 1, p. 6); no operation count, parameter count or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 5: "The datasets were generated independently for each SNR value using random transmitted symbols and channel realizations." The data are self-simulated; the paper gives no link to code or data and uses no public dataset or measured data.
notes: Borderline eligibility: the proposed contribution is a non-learned analysis metric (geometry ratio), and the paper calls the SVM, KNN and neural network evaluation tools (p. 2). Included because these learned classifiers perform the symbol detection and their BER is reported (Figs. 4, 5, 8; Algorithm 1, p. 9); if the reviewer reads them as mere evaluation tools, the code would be no_learning. q3 rests on the BER comparison of classical, SVM, KNN and NN detectors, which the paper does not present as its aim (p. 16), so the reviewer should confirm it. Tables 1 to 4 and Figs. 4 to 9 were read from the PDF pages.
